Virus-like SSL-RNA is considered a strong agonist of pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) such as RIG-I, which can trigger the release of type I interferons and other cytokines, creating a broad-spectrum antiviral state.
Theoretically, SSL-RNA can be used for early control of various RNA virus diseases, including coronaviruses, influenza viruses, henipaviruses, and enteroviruses, as well as some DNA viruses.
In the prevention aspect, SSL-RNA can short-term stimulate a broad-spectrum antiviral state in high-risk exposure populations.
In the treatment aspect, SSL-RNA can be combined with specific antiviral drugs or interferon therapy to shorten virus clearance time and reduce severe cases and mortality.
Overactivation of the immune system by SSL-RNA may cause side effects such as cytokine storms, necessitating precise dosing and targeting.
A challenge for RNA drugs, including SSL-RNA, is the efficient delivery to target cells or tissues while avoiding rapid degradation in the body.
The proposed solution includes lung-targeted broad-spectrum antiviral RNA/LNP therapy.

The project includes a milestone plan with specific tasks and goals over a timeline of 0-36 months.
From 0-6 months, the main tasks include establishing a laboratory and initial team, with goals to complete core team recruitment and initiate project research.
The expected outcome for the 0-6 month milestone is the formal operation of the laboratory and generation of preliminary research results.
From 6-12 months, the focus will be on core technology development and optimization, including technology transfer from domestic teams.
The expected outcome for the 6-12 month milestone is to provide an initial technical validation report and establish cooperation agreements.
From 12-18 months, the project aims to submit clinical trial applications and validate GMP production.
The expected outcome for the 12-18 month milestone includes starting platform services and obtaining initial customer feedback.
From 18-36 months, the project will focus on product launch and market expansion.
The expected outcome for the 18-36 month milestone is the official launch of the product and achieving the targeted market share.
The total budget for the project is approximately 4500万元, allocated in phases to support the entire cycle from R&D to clinical trial applications.
The project requires a laboratory that meets GLP standards, with an area of at least 500 square meters and equipped with BSL-2 facilities.
The project will utilize existing laboratory resources from partners like McGill University and CQIB to reduce initial investment pressure.
The project anticipates additional regulatory consulting costs of approximately 100万元 during the clinical trial application phase.
The project has identified technical development risks related to the optimization of LNP delivery technology.
The project has assembled a research team of world-class experts, including Dr. Zhenlong Liu and Prof. Guojun Chen, to address technical challenges.
The project plans to collaborate with strategic partners like Merck and Fujifilm to leverage existing resources for overcoming technical hurdles.
The project faces market entry risks due to competition in the nucleic acid drug market.
The project aims to provide unique value through low-toxicity LNP technology, which has a significant competitive advantage.
The project plans to establish market influence quickly through existing partner networks and reputations.
The project has identified funding pressure risks due to the high intensity of R&D and clinical trials.
The project has planned a reasonable phased funding requirement and aims to attract long-term strategic investors.
The project has a regulatory approval risk due to the lengthy approval times for clinical trials and product launches.
The project is guided by an experienced regulatory team to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements during clinical trial applications.
